newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices steady, poor mill buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices steady, poor mill buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Thursday held steady at improved levels, dealers said.
Fresh mill buying was dull at a higher level but restricted arrivals, due to the tailend of the season, kept offerings low, they said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi was consolidating gains at 1,050/1,080 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and so was Punjab saw-ginned at 1,830/1,900 rupees and F-414 at 2,040/2,060 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) was steady at 14,300/14,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Sentiments at the close remained firm on expectations that the government may allow fresh export of cotton," one broker said.
Dealers said some state agencies with unsold stock in hand were pressing the Indian government to allow fresh export of at least 100,000/200,000 bales (170 kg each).
